free_tier.stated: No free plan. The plans page lists '1 Year' at '$58' ('$4,8 / month') beside 1 Month '$9', 3 Months '$24' ('$8 / month') and 2 Years '$90'. A trial exists: 'a 1-week trial account for only $2'.
free_tier.notes: The plan links carry a promotion code (OCT26), so the listed prices may be promotional. The trial allows 3 simultaneous connections instead of 6.

retention.stated: not applicable: a tunnel, not stored bytes
retention.notes: The vendor states it does not log or monitor user activity such as visited sites or files transferred; its FAQ also describes the connection logs it keeps.

egress.terms: No speed limit and no byte cap stated: the features list says 'No speed limit', and servers are 'connected to gigabit ports'. The vendor says it does not oversell bandwidth.
egress.free_allowance: none: no free plan; 1-week trial at USD 2

interface_detail: A tunnel and a browser proxy. Protocols: OpenVPN (TCP and UDP on several ports, with XOR and a V2Ray-based TCP obfuscation), IKEv2/IPsec, WireGuard (stated 'in beta' in the FAQ) and L2TP/IPsec. UDP: yes, OpenVPN UDP is offered. Port forwarding: not offered ('No, we don't. We believe it is a risk for the privacy and security of users.'). SOCKS5: unverified: the SecureProxy browser extension is an HTTPS proxy, and the SOCKS5 knowledge-base page returned the vendor's home page; no SOCKS5 endpoint is confirmed. Obfuscation: OpenVPN XOR on TCP 443 and a V2Ray TCP obfuscation layer. BitTorrent: not blocked; advised only on the P2P-optimised locations.
tooling: The vendor's apps (Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, Linux beta) and OpenVPN, WireGuard, IKEv2 or L2TP clients with the account's credentials; SecureProxy browser extensions for Chrome and Firefox.
chaining: A tunnel exit: the vendor states it provides shared IP addresses only, so the upstream sees an address shared with every user on the node.

limits.value: shared addresses: 'all users connected to the same VPN node will use the same IP addresses'; no dedicated IP is sold
6 simultaneous connections with OpenVPN or IPsec plus 6 with WireGuard (12 in total); the trial allows 3

limits_note: The connection counts are filed under request-rate because the vocabulary has no concurrent-connection kind. The P2P guidance names seven locations (Canada - Toronto, Sweden, Netherlands, Finland, Switzerland, France, Romania) and the 28 gigabit servers in them.
binding_note: No byte quota or rate is published; the shared-address model and the connection counts are stated, and the vocabulary cannot rank them against a quota.

identity_cost.detail: unverified: the checkout and sign-up form are behind a sign-up and were not read; the FAQ says the vendor sends auto-generated payment reminders and confirmations to customers, and accepts Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, PayPal, cards and vouchers. The email kind is the structured value inferred from the payment reminders; no phone, card or ID requirement is stated on the pages read.

reliability_note: The FAQ says accounts are activated when the payment is confirmed; the vendor keeps connection logs described in its FAQ (connection start and end) and states it does not log activity.
confidence_note: Documented: price, protocols, UDP, port-forwarding refusal, obfuscation and the BitTorrent line are quoted from the vendor's plans page, FAQ and knowledge base. Identity is inferred, not read, because the checkout is behind a sign-up. Nothing was connected through the service.
price_per_tb_month: USD 58 for 1 year; a subscription price, not a per-TB price
